transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess people are just starting to notice that I can't really... sit and listen. I keep getting up when I'm supposed to just stay put. Like during client interviews, or tutoring sessions... even my book club. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
Can you tell me if this difficulty staying still and focused has been present since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... no, it's not new. It's... always been there, I guess. 

If you looked at my grade-school report cards, they always said I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. My mother actually still brings it up sometimes. She jokes that I treated every classroom like a... like a crime scene I had to pace through. 

So... yeah. Since I was a kid.
Besides having trouble staying seated, do you also find it hard to keep your attention on tasks, tend to lose track of details, or forget things often, even when you're not moving around?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I lose track of details or forget things. I mean, my memory is fine. It's... it's really just what I mentioned before. The staying put.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in other situations?

Um... I suppose. Sometimes. 

Like... at work, if I hear the junior detectives discussing a lead, I might... jump in. Just start giving advice or asking questions before they've actually asked for my input. Or... if a neighbor is talking out in the hallway, I'll do the same thing. 

I don't really mean to, I just... it's only afterward that I realize I completely barged into someone else's conversation. So... yes. I guess I do that.
Would you say these behaviors—getting up when you should stay seated, jumping into conversations—have actually caused problems for you, like at work, in relationships, or in other areas of your life?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. 

It's... it's been an issue at work lately. I guess I've... irritated a few clients. And the junior detectives, they don't really want to debrief with me as much anymore. They say I... steamroll them. 

And... well, I have missed a few details on some investigations because of it. So... yeah. It's causing some problems.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (childhood-onset) pattern of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms—motor restlessness with inability to remain seated, and impulsive interrupting/blurting in conversations—without significant inattentive symptoms (denies forgetfulness or losing track of details). Symptoms are pervasive across multiple settings (work, tutoring, book club, social interactions) and have caused clear functional impairment (strained work relationships, missed case details, client irritation). This pattern is consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation, persisting into adulthood. Antisocial personality traits and mood disorder were considered but not supported, as there is no evidence of disregard for others' rights, mood episodes, or affective symptoms—impulsivity is limited to attention/activity regulation rather than broader personality or mood pathology.
